description: Verify the Protocol Type field of DUT's emitted ARP Request equals ARP_PROTOCOL_IP (0x0800) — names the upper-layer protocol whose address is being resolved (RFC 826 packet generation)
approach:
[Objective]
The Protocol Type field of an ARP Request announces which upper-layer protocol family the target_ip / sender_ip fields belong to. For IPv4, that is 0x0800. This case provokes a DUT ARP Request and asserts the field value.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. (No cache seeding — DUT's cache for HOST-1-IP starts empty.)

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message
   ⇒ DUT unicast-Nacks back to HOST-1-IP; cache miss forces an ARP Request.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request
      - opcode      == 1
      - sender_mac  == DUT iface MAC
      - target_ip   == HOST-1-IP
      - proto_type  == 0x0800 (ARP_PROTOCOL_IP)   ← key check

[Pass condition]
The observed ARP Request's Protocol Type equals 0x0800.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_proto_type — ARP Request seen but Protocol Type was not 0x0800 (upper-layer family mislabelled)
• Fail_timeout — No ARP Request observed within the window

verdicts.Fail_proto_type: ARP Request emitted but proto_type was not 0x0800 — upper-layer family mismatch
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT ARP Request observed within the window
